topics.name: session_state
topics.definition: Session State allows sharing variables between script reruns within a user session, enabling stateful data management in Streamlit apps.

topics.name: widget_state_management
topics.definition: Widget state management covers how Streamlit widgets retain their values across reruns and the implications of using `st.session_state` for state persistence.

topics.name: form_submission
topics.definition: Form submission in Streamlit allows users to group inputs and submit them all at once, triggering a rerun of the script with updated values.

topics.name: caching_mechanism
topics.definition: The caching mechanism in Streamlit helps store results of slow function calls to improve app performance and manage object persistence across reruns.

topics.name: navigation_in_multipage_apps
topics.definition: Navigation in multipage apps allows users to define and manage available pages, facilitating dynamic updates and user interaction.

topics.name: widget_behavior
topics.definition: Widget behavior encompasses how different Streamlit widgets function, including their return values, callback functionality, and session dependency.

topics.name: app_testing
topics.definition: App testing in Streamlit involves verifying user interactions and state management to ensure app reliability and correctness.

topics.name: serialization_constraints
topics.definition: Serialization constraints address the limitations and security risks associated with using Python's `pickle` module for object serialization in Streamlit.

topics.name: displaying_dataframes
topics.definition: Displaying dataframes in Streamlit involves rendering pandas DataFrames using `st.dataframe` and `st.table`, with options for interactivity and static views.

topics.name: unexpected_widget_behavior
topics.definition: Unexpected widget behavior refers to issues where widgets do not function as intended, such as losing state or failing to respond to changes.

topics.name: asynchronous_code_issues
topics.definition: Asynchronous code issues involve problems encountered when using asynchronous programming patterns with Streamlit, particularly regarding session state.

topics.name: fragment_behavior
topics.definition: Fragment behavior describes how reusable components interact with the main app, including state management and rerun implications.

topics.name: data_editor_behavior
topics.definition: Data editor behavior explains how `st.data_editor` allows users to edit dataframes interactively, tracking changes through `st.session_state`.

topics.name: form_limitations
topics.definition: Form limitations in Streamlit detail the constraints and requirements for using forms, including restrictions on nested forms and widget interactions.

topics.name: widget_interaction_order
topics.definition: Widget interaction order describes the sequence of operations that occur when a user interacts with a widget, including state updates and callback executions.

topics.name: other
topics.definition: none of the other topics, or too mixed to pick one
